title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: draft timing, deemed approval and pre-issuance draft rounds
content:
## Scope

This card lists, for each Bills of Lading and Transport Documents type, the three values that govern the draft stage: the service standard for sending the draft after the shipping instructions are received, the hours after which an unanswered draft is deemed approved, and the maximum number of pre-issuance corrections (draft reopenings) allowed on one document.

## Tier table

| Document type | Draft sent within (hours after shipping instructions received) | Unanswered draft deemed approved after (hours from sending) | Maximum pre-issuance draft rounds per document |
|---|---|---|---|
| AHL Sea Waybill | 12 | 48 | 5 |
| AHL Electronic Bill of Lading | 6 | 48 | 5 |
| AHL Straight Bill of Lading | 12 | 24 | 4 |
| AHL Negotiable Bill of Lading | 12 | 24 | 4 |
| AHL Combined Transport Bill of Lading | 24 | 24 | 4 |
| AHL Switch Bill of Lading | 24 | 24 | 3 |

## Questions answered by the table

**How quickly is an AHL Electronic Bill of Lading draft sent?** Within 6 hours of the shipping instructions being received, the shortest standard of any type.

**After how long is an AHL Straight Bill of Lading draft deemed approved if the shipper does not answer?** After 24 hours from the draft being sent.

**How many times may an AHL Switch Bill of Lading draft be reopened before issuance?** The limit is 3 rounds per document, against 5 on the AHL Sea Waybill and the AHL Electronic Bill of Lading and 4 on the other types.

## Hypothetical illustration

A hypothetical AHL Sea Waybill draft sent on a Monday at 09:00 that receives no answer from the shipper reaches the 48-hour mark on the Wednesday at 09:00.
